$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},
$\,{X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-2}}.
q-322280.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+3L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1={X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+3=-{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
s{X}_{1}(s)-1={X}_{1}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{1}{s-1}.
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
s{X}_{2}(s)+3=-(\frac{1}{s-1})+3{X}_{2}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{-3s+2}{(s-1)(s-3)}.
$$

By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{5}{s-2},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{5}{s-2}+\frac{2}{s+1}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{5}{s-2}\} \\  & =5\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}\} \\  & =5{e}^{2\cdot t} \\  & =5{e}^{2t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{5}{s-2}+\frac{2}{s+1}\} \\  & =5\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}\}+2\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s+1}\} \\  & =5{e}^{2\cdot t}+2{e}^{-1\cdot t} \\  & =5{e}^{2t}+2{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2t} \\ 5{e}^{2t}+2{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$
